[ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively, the command may have been issued separately and summarized, as in the address to the messengers to eat good things. | mentions 23:51

[ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Some take it to address only Adam and Eve, since the same story says ‘both of you descend’; the plural can stand for descendants because they are humanity’s source. | mentions 2:38

[ALUSI-FULL:v8p102/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · محمد بن قيس | reports | Muḥammad ibn Qays relates that Adam blamed Eve, she blamed the serpent, and the serpent blamed Iblīs; God assigned Eve monthly bleeding, the serpent to crawl and be struck in the face, and cursed Iblīs.
[ELMALILI:7:23-25/r6] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The descent assigns them an earthly dwelling and provision for a limited time, amid enmity among them.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The clause about having a settled place on earth is coordinated with the preceding clause that some are enemies to others.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | مستقر is a mimetic verbal noun meaning remaining or staying; Ibn Ashur points to the same word in two other verses. | mentions 6:67, 6:98
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · بعض المفسرين | rejects | Some exegetes took the settled place to mean burial, but Ibn Ashur rejects this because enjoyment is mentioned and jinn and devils are not buried in the earth.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | متاع and تمتع mean gaining nonlasting pleasures and desires; متاع can also denote the things from which one benefits. | mentions 4:102
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | حين means a period, long or short; it is indefinite here because its duration varies among kinds and individuals.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#2/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The period is the life in which a being can perceive pleasures and persist as a living self; this divinely determined term ends with life, ending settled existence and enjoyment, and is neither favor nor punishment.
[TABATABAI:7:20-25/r8] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The address appears to include Adam, his wife, and Iblis; their mutual enmity is seen in their differing natures, and the earthly dwelling and provision last until worldly life ends.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Though God accepted Adam and Eve’s repentance, divine wisdom sent them from Paradise to earth for a contest against Satan and his progeny; Paradise became the reward for those who prevail. | mentions 2:30, 2:31, 2:32, 2:33, 2:34, 2:35, 2:36, 2:37, 2:38, 2:39
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The phrase “enemies of one another” casts Adam and Iblīs as opposing parties: Satan may lead Adam’s descendants astray, while they can regain Paradise by defeating his designs.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Adam and Eve repented after recognizing their sin; God accepted their repentance, as 2:37 says, then sent them to the world as a place of testing. | mentions 2:37
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Together with 2:36, 2:38, and 20:123, these verses show Adam and Eve were expelled from Paradise because of their sin, an event that shaped humanity’s fate. | mentions 2:36, 2:38, 20:123
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The Torah’s account that Adam and Eve also faced other hardships is absent from the Qur’an.

[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The move from first sin and expulsion marks humanity’s moral rise into a free, accountable kind of being able to err, repent, and consciously choose goodness, not a moral decline.
